html:
Sephardic Jews, descendants of those expelled from Spain in 1492, settled in Sarajevo by 1565 and built one of the main Jewish communities of the Ottoman Balkans.

They came by way of Salonica and other Ottoman cities, spoke Ladino and worked as traders, craftsmen and doctors. Sarajevo's old synagogue dates from 1581. Ashkenazi Jews arrived under Austrian rule after 1878. The community's best known treasure is the Sarajevo Haggadah, an illuminated manuscript made in Spain in the 1300s, brought here by refugees and later saved from the Nazis and again during the siege of the 1990s. In the Holocaust the Ustaše and the Germans killed most of the roughly 14,000 Jews of Bosnia.
sum: Sephardic Jews, descendants of those expelled from Spain in 1492, settled in Sarajevo by 1565 and built one of the main Jewish communities of the Ottoman Balkans.
